settings.out_of_scope_reason: Reward distributions of all arms are modulated by a common unobserved finite-state Markov chain (hidden Markov / POMDP structure); Markovian environments are out of scope in this ontology version.
unmapped: Rewards of all arms modulated by a common hidden finite-state Markov chain with unknown transition matrix P (regime switching); the state is never observed
Regret benchmarked against the optimal long-run average reward rho* of the belief-MDP (POMDP) oracle that knows P and the reward distributions but not the state
Learner knows the number of hidden states M
Learner needs (upper bounds on) the spectral-estimator constants C_1, C_2
Assumes access to an optimization oracle solving the average-reward belief-MDP Bellman equation
Transition matrix P invertible, mean reward matrix full row rank, min entry of P epsilon > 0
settings.definition_quote: There is a Markov chain $\{M_t\}$ with states $\mathcal{M}\coloneqq\{1,2,\dots,M\}$ and transition probability matrix $P$. In period $t$, if the state of the Markov chain $M_t=m$ and the agent chooses arm $I_t= i$, then the reward in that period is $R_t$ ... distribution $Q(\cdot|m,i)$. The agent knows $M$ and $I$, but has no knowledge about the underlying state $M_t$, the transition matrix $P$ or the reward distribution ... $\mathcal{R}_T\coloneqq T\rho^* - \sum_{t=1}^T R_t^{\pi}$.

source.label: thm:upper_bound
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions 1 to 3 hold. Fix the parameter $\tau_1$ in Algorithm 2 to be sufficiently large. Then there exist constants $T_0,C$ which are independent of $T$, such that when $T>T_0$, with probability $1-\frac{7}{2}\delta$, the regret of Algorithm~2 satisfies $\mathcal{R}_T \leq CT^{2/3}\sqrt{\log\left(\frac{3(S+1)}{\delta}T\right)}+T_0\rho^*$, where $S=2I$ ...

results.notes: Paper's S=2I with I = number of arms (K). Regret is realized regret T rho* - sum R_t bounded w.p. 1-7delta/2. Constant C given explicitly in paper; computation of optimistic POMDP not addressed efficiently.

symbols.C_reg: constant independent of T (as in Theorem 1)
symbols.T_0: number of periods for exploration samples to exceed N_0

conditions: Assumption 2: mean reward matrix full row rank
Assumption 3: min entry of P epsilon > 0

source.label: thm:expected_upper_bound
source.quote: Under the same assumptions as Theorem~\ref{thm:upper_bound}, the regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:SEEU} satisfies $\E[\mathcal{R}_T] \leq CT^{2/3}\sqrt{2\log T} + (T_0+11(S+1))\rho^*$.

results.notes: Obtained by choosing delta = 3(S+1)/T, which uses T, so marked known horizon. Expected regret E[T rho* - sum R_t] relative to the POMDP oracle's average reward.
